doc.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Metronome All-Stars 1947 and his first bebop solo on Leap Here
summary: He thinks his solo on Leap Here was his first recorded bebop solo, though he cannot recall the personnel.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: So in ’47 you had your second Metronome All-Stars session and I think that that you were credited with your first true bebop solo on that session. Is that, would you say that? On Leap Here.
Wow, I can’t. Oh yeah, Leap Here, right…
Would you consider that your first… DeFranco:…and Metronome Riff.
Would you consider that your first real bebop solo?
Wow, I recorded, yeah, I guess so—first recorded bebop solo.
Do you remember who the other people on that session?
No, no, not really because I did so many of those sessions and all the guys that were on those sessions kind of get mixed up after so many years. Like…
I wonder if we can find it.
You have to fish through a sea of Tommy Dorsey recordings to find it, there’s Boyd Raeburn. So Metronome All-Stars, no that’s later, that’s ’49.
